newsitem.title: INDIA: Anti-Pakistan protesters, police clash in Delhi.
newsitem.headline: Anti-Pakistan protesters, police clash in Delhi.

text.p: A few protesters and some policemen were injured on Thursday when police used water cannon to disperse a 1,000-strong crowd protesting outside Pakistan's embassy in the Indian capital, eyewitnesses said.

Supporters of the youth wing of the former ruling Congress party were protesting against what they called Pakistan's support for Moslem separatists in Kashmir on the eve of the resumption of talks between arch-rivals India and Pakistan.
Senior Indian and Pakistani diplomats are due to resume talks in New Delhi on Friday after a gap of nearly three years.
"Some policemen and protesters have been injured," said a police official at the Chanakyapuri district police station.
"Police used water cannon to disperse a crowd of around 1,000 people when they tried to break through the security cordon and some of them sustained minor injuries," said one eyewitness.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars, two of them over Kashmir, since their independence from Britain in 1947.
India accuses Pakistan of providing arms and material support to a seven-year-old Moslem revolt in Kashmir, a charge denied by Islamabad.
